title: "penguins in class"
format: html

```{r}
options(scipen = 10)
library(tidyverse)
library(bayesrules)
library(rstanarm)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggExtra)
library(report)
data <- bayesrules::penguins_bayes

```

```{r}
ggplot(data=data, aes(x = flipper_length_mm, fill = species))+
  geom_histogram()
```

the flipper length histogram has 2 bell shapes which are probably from the most common species in the data set having a range of flipper lengths

```{r}
ggplot(data=data, aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_length_mm))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")+
  stat_cor()
```

```{r}
p <- ggplot(data=data, aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_length_mm))+
  geom_point()

ggMarginal(p, type = "density", groupfill = TRUE)

```

the graph here is pretty positive

.

```{r}
m0 <- 200   # centered intercept mean
s0 <- 10.2   # centered intercept SD
m1 <- 3.5   # slope mean
s1 <- 1.02   # slope SD
l  <- .08   # sigma's exponential rate
```

```{r}
plot_normal(200, 10.2)
```

```{r}
plot_normal(3.5,1.02)
```

```{r}
plot_gamma(1, 0.08)
```

```{r}
model <- stan_glm(
  flipper_length_mm ~ bill_length_mm, data = data,
  family = gaussian,
  prior_intercept = normal(m0, s0),
  prior = normal(m1, s1),
  prior_aux = exponential(l),
  chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 84735
)
```

```{r}
model
```

```{r}
summary(model)
```

```{r}
report::report(model)
```

```{r}
posterior <- as.data.frame(model)
beta0c_draws <- posterior$`(Intercept)` + posterior$bill_length_mm * mean(data$bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)

```

using machine learning to predict the winning score of of pga tour events

<https://norma.ncirl.ie/2493/1/oisinwiseman.pdf#page=2.83>

<https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/cviaxmiwnptr/pga-tour-results-2001-to-may-2024/data>

```{r}
median(posterior$`(Intercept)`)
median(posterior$bill_length_mm)
```

flipper_length_mm = intercept of bill length_mm + slope of the graph for bill_length_mm × bill_length_mm.

```{r}
quantile(posterior$bill_length_mm, c(0.05, 0.95))
```

There is a 90% probability that for every 1mm increase in a penguin's bill length, their flipper length increases by between 1.5 mm and 1.87 mm.

```{r}
quantile(beta0c_draws, c(0.05, 0.95))
```

there is a 90% probability that a penguin with an average bill length will have a flipper length between 199.9 mm and 201.86 mm.

```{r}
mean(posterior$bill_length_mm > 0)
```

this tells us what the probability of the slope being positive is and the p value tells us how surprising it is if the slope is 0

```{r}
summary(model)[, c("Rhat", "n_eff")]

```

since all of the Rhat values are close to 1 this tells us that the chain worked properly and the posterior is accurate.

```{r}
lm(flipper_length_mm ~ bill_length_mm, data = data)
```

```{r}
median(posterior$`(Intercept)`)
median(posterior$bill_length_mm)
```

they are very similar so a linear model would work better for this use case because it is much faster and will still give us very similar results.
